skill.name: coverage-analyzer
skill.description: Analyze test coverage reports, identify uncovered code paths, and suggest practical tests to improve project quality.
skill.summary: Find coverage gaps and plan targeted tests for Python projects.
skill.author: Atyantik

content.value_statement: Teams need clear coverage insight before they can improve tests. This skill turns coverage reports into prioritized gaps, test ideas, and next actions.
actual_capabilities: Reviews coverage output and highlights files below the target.
Groups uncovered lines by criticality, including errors and edge cases.
Suggests specific tests for uncovered functions and branches.
Summarizes coverage by module with priority and impact.
Tracks coverage changes and identifies regressions over time.
limitations: Requires an existing coverage report or permission to run coverage tools.
Recommendations depend on readable source code and test structure.
Does not guarantee bug-free code or complete behavioral coverage.
Package installation examples should be approved before running.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Feature for Review
use_cases.description: Find missing tests before opening a pull request and focus on changed code first.

use_cases.title: Raise Coverage Above a Gate
use_cases.description: Prioritize quick tests that move a project above an 80 percent coverage target.

use_cases.title: Monitor Test Quality Trends
use_cases.description: Review coverage history and identify modules that are losing test protection.

prompt_templates.title: Review Current Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the latest coverage report. Show total coverage, files below target, and the first tests I should write.

prompt_templates.title: Find Critical Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Find critical uncovered code paths. Focus on validation, authorization, error handling, and edge cases.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Tests for a Module
prompt_templates.prompt: Review coverage for this module and suggest focused tests with scenario names, expected behavior, and priority.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Coverage Recovery Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare current coverage with recent history. Create a prioritized plan to recover regressions and pass the coverage gate.

output_examples.input: A project is at 75 percent coverage and needs to reach 80 percent.
output_examples.output: The report identifies the largest gaps, estimates coverage impact, and recommends the fastest tests to reach the target.

output_examples.input: A validator module has uncovered exception handling paths.
output_examples.output: The analysis marks the paths as critical and proposes tests for invalid input, unexpected errors, and expected failures.

output_examples.input: Coverage has stalled across recent weeks.
output_examples.output: The trend summary highlights unchanged modules, likely blockers, and a short action plan for restoring progress.

best_practices: Run the normal project coverage command before asking for analysis.
Start with high-risk uncovered code before improving low-risk helpers.
Review suggested tests for project style and meaningful assertions.
anti_patterns: Do not add tests only to execute lines without checking behavior.
Do not ignore uncovered error handling in public interfaces.
Do not install new coverage tools without approval from the project owner.

faq.question: Does this skill run coverage automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide coverage commands, but execution depends on the agent and user approval.

faq.question: Which projects work best with it?
faq.answer: It is written for Python projects that use common coverage reports and pytest workflows.

faq.question: Can it write the tests for me?
faq.answer: It suggests concrete test scenarios and examples. The agent can implement tests when the user requests code changes.

faq.question: Does 100 percent coverage mean the code is safe?
faq.answer: No. The skill stresses meaningful tests, critical paths, and behavior checks over raw percentages.

faq.question: Can it analyze coverage trends?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare saved coverage history and call out regressions or stalled progress.

faq.question: Does it require internet access?
faq.answer: No for normal analysis. One optional example mentions installing a helper tool, which may need network access.
